text_en: All over Ethiopia, when people want sparkling water, they simply ask for Ambo.
But Ambo is not a bottle. It is a town, a few hours west of Addis Ababa. This is the road there.
The minibus leaves before sunrise, and the city falls away behind the eucalyptus trees.
The land opens up. Farmers are already in their fields, and the hills fold into more hills.
Every bend in the road brings the mountains a little closer.
Then the town appears. Quiet streets, students walking to class, the smell of rain on red earth.
Under Ambo, the ground is warm. Water rises from deep below, full of bubbles: the same water the whole country drinks.
I drink it here, at the source. It tastes the same, and completely different.
So the next time you order an Ambo, remember: it is not just water. It is a place.
